BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Status:** Internal analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team. Every item below is a departure from our playbook unless marked otherwise. The Seller's "key negotiated positions," "fair and balanced," and "agreed price mechanics" language does not clear anything. Under playbook sec 6.3, none of these positions is treated as agreed until it passes our own authority process.

## 1. Most material departures

**(a) Fundamental/Title claims are pulled into the general regime (Seller: "administrative simplicity").**
This is the most serious issue. Our playbook requires a separate Fundamental/Title regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the basket, de minimis, or knowledge bar. The Seller's proposal would put capacity and title under the 20% cap and 18-month limit. Given that the Seller's own title evidence is an internal share register (DL §10), this exposure is real. Reject outright.

**(b) Sweeping "any limitation applies to all Claims" language (Clause 12.3/13) and limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions applying to "all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5).**
This is a hidden general-regime override. It would also reach fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, which our playbook carves out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable and without any waiver. The Seller's draft contains no fraud carve-out at all. Require an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out and keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate.

**(c) Economic terms for general warranty claims are well outside our position.**

| Term | Seller | Playbook | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start) | 20% is a conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Claims under AUD 25k are unrecoverable under the Seller's draft. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Seller's version is roughly five times our basket and changes the mechanics. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. None given. |

Note that the Seller's 4.8m figure matches our fallback number. That is a coincidence to be aware of, not a clearance. Under sec 6.3, a proposed change is not cleared because one number matches a fallback.

**(d) Blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion (Clause 8.3).**
The Seller would bar claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure, this would effectively remove most of the warranty protection. The playbook requires deletion. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**(e) Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure (Schedule 7; DL §§1.1–1.2).**
The Seller would disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (through 5pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Reject both paragraphs.

## 2. Specific transaction issues

**Bluefen (Clause 3/6.3; DL §2; DD-002).**
The Seller would use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent. The playbook requires effective consent plus evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. The exposure is significant: about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%). The DL confirms no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions. Reject consent-on-delivery and make this a Completion condition, not a post-Completion deliverable.

**Riverlark (Clauses 2/7; DL §3; DD-003).**
The Seller would provide a release "following Completion." The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The ~AUD 3.2m figure comes from DD-003 and is now stale (the data room date is 22 September, and today is 5 November). Obtain a current payoff letter and confirm that the funds flow actually deducts it. The Seller says the funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics," which does not confirm a debt payoff line.

**Employee bonuses (DL §5; DD-005).**
The AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the funds flow and described as "a matter for the Seller." The playbook requires that the amount be either a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, and that it not be silently excluded. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unquantified in the disclosure. Require a specific line item or Seller funding, including on-costs, and a confirmed list of the employees and triggering conditions.

**Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL §4; DD-004/DD-010).**
The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." The playbook requires broadening the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open amount in DD-010 is not independently verified in either direction, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Ask for bank evidence of non-payment and the cure mechanics. Do not accept "adequate."

**Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6/Schedule 6; DL §6; DD-006).**
The Seller calls it "a preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Our playbook assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The Seller's own DL also says the investigation is preliminary and does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope (about 1,240 records), or whether notification is required. Require preservation of logs, a investigation timetable, and regular written updates. Do not accept the "not material" characterisation as a finding. Whether a specific indemnity is warranted is a judgement call for the deal team and is not set out in the playbook.

**Sandbar renewals (DL §8; DD-008/DD-011).**
The Seller calls the three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) "ordinary-course operating costs." The DL says the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook requires assessment and rules out automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. Check whether DD-008 and DD-011 overlap, since the DL says to read them together. Assess before taking a position.

**Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime").**
Our playbook keeps these categories open, with no resolution and no assumed unlimited liability. Reject folding them into the general regime.

**Title (Seller: DD-012 share register "evidences" title).**
The playbook treats DD-012 as an internal supplied source, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority: ASIC current company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, a certified share register, and the executed share transfer or equivalent. The DL itself (§10) confirms the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**Office lease (DL §7; DD-007) and Mossvale (DL §9; DD-009).**
The playbook has no specific position on these. The DL says neither document establishes that landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. Do not accept "not required" as a fact. Obtain the legal analysis, and if consent is needed, treat it as a Completion deliverable. DL §1.4 also contains non-admission language. It is not a reason to close the point.

## 3. Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the Seller's draft as a basis for negotiation.** Our opening position stays at 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, and 24 months. The 20%/AUD 4.8m and 18-month fallbacks are not authorised. Any movement requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the specific draft.
2. **Separate Fundamental/Title** into its own regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. **Require an express, non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. Delete "any limitation applies to all Claims."
4. **Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion** (Clause 8.3). Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry.
5. **Reject whole-data-room, Accounts and public-register disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
7. **Riverlark:** current payoff letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180k independently.
10. **DD-006 export incident:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Accept no characterisation of the incident as immaterial, and no characterisation as a confirmed breach.
11. **Sandbar renewals:** assess (check for overlap between DD-008 and DD-011). No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
12. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from the general regime.
13. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
14. **Office lease and Mossvale:** obtain a legal view on whether consent is needed, and treat any required consent as a Completion deliverable.
15. **Refresh all facts.** The data-room figures are as at 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November 2026. Refresh Bluefen status, the Riverlark payoff, bonus eligibility, the DD-006 investigation status, Ironquay payments, and Sandbar terms before taking positions.

**Governance point:** Nothing in the Seller's letter is cleared. Any change that departs from the playbook needs Amelia Frost's written authority before we concede it, even if the number matches a fallback.
